title: MZ Llewl and the Lyre of Two Worlds

posts.author: padr81
posts.body:
Latest
Patch 0.1.3.1 is here and comes with over 80 bug fixes, tweaks, changes and updates and an all new graphical style.
Thanks to everyone who has already played or offered feedback on the demo, you guys are amazing and the game already feels 100 times better.  Y'all are amazing.  Thank you so much.
Click here to see bug fixes and game tweaks.
About
Spoiler
Llewl is a love letter to the classic JRPG's of the 90's but with many modern design principles, the goal is to create a jRPG that plays like 2023 but hits square in the nostalgia like its 1996.
Join trainee Guardian Sarah and her best friend Hans as they go on an epic adventure to rescue her childhood love Llewl.  Joined by a diverse team of characters along the way, the game has one goal, to see you the player play through with a smile on your face at all time.

posts.author: SpiralSigil
posts.body:
So I just played through part of the demo, and as a fellow game maker, as well as a reviewer and streamer, I streamed my experience to some of my community, and we kind of just had a blast going through it, discussing game design stuff as well as things that were really good and things that could use some improvement. Not in a bad way - I honestly dont think there was anything I saw or experienced that was actually BAD or INCORRECT - But purely in a constructive way. If youre at all curious how I reacted to the demo (At least what I played through before I had to leave) here;
That said, to summarize, the game has really solid potential. You have good mapping skills, some features are just great and little details I didnt even consider despite using a lot of the same assets. So I would be happy to stream more of this.

posts.author: TESTOSTERONE
posts.body:
Spoiler:
Positives
(+) The 3-d like beginning was great, you knew something was about to go down.
(+) I did not expect swimming, and then when I realized I could swim it was like woaaaaah, neat!
(+) Snow bros are too cute
And the boss fights were challenging and well balanced.
(++) I appreciate the humor, and the game is true to its word - it made me smile several times. Characters say some funny stuff, especially the Blade and his mouth. Go trainee guardian Sarah!
(+) The combinations / limit breaks (whatever they are) are frigging awesome during fight when they come up. Great job there, including the battle animations.
(+) Exploration felt rewarding, especially since I was a little bit lost wondering around the big maps.
(+) The graphics are well done. And the pixel art animations/poses, great job!
(+) Heal on level up is always appreciated.
(+) After defeating the boss... all the treasures chests that were there to restock the items I used and to reward me <3
(+) Unreadable scrolls were kind of a cool idea. And once they are translated into stat boosting scrolls I am so glad it's applied to ALL party members, instead of me having to pick one.
(+) Mini games are something different and I kind of liked them.  Although, for the singing mini game, maybe I can "tune" my lute first as practice since I didn't know what to expect and missed the first keyboard press.
Spoiler:
Improvements / Suggestions
(-) I wish you could save everywhere. I thought about disabling save in dungeons too, but in this day and age...  it just isn't necessary and people appreciate being able to hop in and out of the game whenever they need.
(-) Mouse on Equip screen did not work, you have to hit enter first before you can select equipment.
(=) I get it's a demo, so I imagine you will add some tutorials for combat, that would be appreciated. Thankfully the guild gave some hints, like guarding restores mana for example.
(=) Character motivations are a bit questionable, but what the heck.... as long as the character banter is fun, it doesn't matter much.
(=) I would like to see more cut scenes and character interactions. Dungeon maps feel big and the balance heavily favors exploration and combat rather than the character banter, which I wanted to see more of.
Spoiler:
Bugs
Battle encounters sometime wouldn't activate on event touch.
I was jumping as I was floating down the water stream in that mini game and then it just kinda kept going and going without any obstacles appearing... I think I broke it.  And that is a shame because my last save was from before entering the cave and I did not want to fight the bosses again.
Spoiler:
Spelling Mistakes
Mayor guard:
you are exhuasted (I think it was mispelled)
want to save save your friend
theres a good chance we can catch them there
TL;DR:
I am not sure the screenshots you have do it justice. This was a pretty fun game and the project has a lot of potential! Please keep the humor. Writing funny/witty dialogue is WAY harder than anything else. As long as you can keep this vibe going, it'll be a good one. I recommend people give this demo a try.

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
I wasn't officially his composer. I told him that I believe in his product and since he often complained about the quality of the music packs, I offered to do a couple tracks for him to show my support.
He wanted me to do more, but 1) It was already like pulling teeth for him to actually like my work (that I did for free). It took a community poll and his jam game before he was finally convinced that my work was fitting. 2) I don't really have the time to work on someone else's game since I barely have time to work on my own game.
If he was easier to work with, I wouldn't mind occasionally doing a bonus song again once every 3 months like yourself...
I like the dude, couldn't ask for a more honest person in my court, but damn is he impossible to please.
Anyways, I'll see what I can do. I'm interested in playing it. Watch out, knowing you're a musician, I might be pretty critical of your soundtrack.

posts.author: padr81
posts.body:
So I kinda forgot this place exists and the last few months have been insane, lots of stuff I can and can't talk about game development wise but the game has got a bit of a makeover...
First up, new graphic style.
We have moved to assets from Seleil the Shaper and imho the game looks much stronger for it.
Here's some shiny new screenshots...
First up is the wonderful new title screen logo from Nowis337.
Here's an in-game shot from the town of Quilt.
(Yes that little discord logo in the bottom right is part of the game.)
And a screenshot from the rewritten intro, where a lot of the jokiness has been removed for a more serious tone.
I'm rewriting the soundtrack as it fell into a weird middle ground between what I vsts I had and the vibe I wanted which satisfied no one.  For the next demo though it'll be placeholders from BitByBit sound.
The combat now has tutorials explaining how systems work so people will understand what's going on, though the super easy intro section remains where a person can just sleep through early encounters.
Also in progress is removing a lot of plugin fluff.
So thanks everyone for the feedback there was tons and hopefully next update will be soon and I'll have more time to spend on these forums going forward.

August 2024 Update.
The last couple of months have been spent on iterating, iterating over an absolute mountain of feedback and slowly adding content from later in the game that isn't in the demo.
Working under the hood on a new tutorial system to replace Visu's plugin, a new controller/keyboard input system (thanks to Neo Soul Gamer) and a OoT styled ocarina system (albeit early days on that one).
Here's a funny video of Yorkshire Pud playing the latest tester demo which feels dated by now, but its  such a funny video and I spent as much time laughing as taking notes (there was lots of notes) I just had to post the link.
He really drove home the point that I have to deal with all the Visu options plugin superfluous fluff at some stage and I need to stop being lazy with that aspect of the game in the most comedic of ways.
Great video and I really enjoyed it, hope you guys do too.

posts.author: RCXGaming
posts.body:
Hello,
@padr81
! I wanted to cover Llewl ever since
@TheAM-Dol
covered it on his stream. The Feedback Festival helped push me to make this review, but I was curious to experience it for myself due to the work you put in.
(Also, the game’s name never fails to make me crack up. Sorry.)
I played to the end of the demo.
--
Spoiler:
Llewl Review
Spoiler:
Pros
+
Extremely pretty title screen - Nowis337 did a great job. Really love the snow effect + the music is very soothing.
+
Oh wow you actually have keyboard rebinding in MZ!! Oh, and gamepad rebinding too. You’re really thinking ahead here.
+
I do like that MZ games tend to come with an autosave function.
+
These overworld sprites and the tilesets are pristine. Kind of remind me of golden era JRPGs. Interesting that they’re also used for combat – very Chrono Trigger of you.
+
I also like how each gal has special situation sprites (eg. sitting down, hugging, etc.)
+
It’s always interesting whenever a tutorial has these effects where they darken parts of the screen to emphasize different UI elements in combat.
+
Oooh! Very good to hear the majority of sound effects aren’t the RTP. I heard Sword2 or something in a cutscene, but that can be easily fixed.
+
Dang, Grandpa is a badass! Oh. Oh  he got burned in a full screen CG.
+
I do like that when Hans says the village was burned to the ground, we actually do get to see it, complete with people actually fighting each other. Helps provide context.
+
Big props to giving our heroes a motive at the start, even if it is just “Rescue Llewl”.
+
Big fan of the snow field theme, it and the gorgeous tileset really does set up the appropriate mood.
+
You can jump and swim in this!? Pretty sick! Also, I like how trying to jump next to an inaccessible space hobbles your character. As well as how you skip bodies of water if your jump goes over them. Really good small detail, I can see speedrunners really enjoying this.
+
Very cool how your character turns semi-translucent when under a bridge. Curious how you did that.
+
This combat system is pretty sick once you understand how it works. The positioning mechanic is incredibly interesting because it forces you to think about the environment instead of just smacking the enemy to death and calling it a day.
The thing I liked the most was how the ice bird boss had the panels light up with little angry icons to show you its attack range when it swoops. That’s cool.
However...
Spoiler:
Observations
=
I do think it’s odd that the text boxes are so big yet there’s barely enough text in them most of the time. I think it’d be better to have smaller text boxes that float over the characters’ heads.
=
Oh… Llewl is a person…?
=
I can see the Chrono Trigger influence from a mile away with that soundfont. Very cheeky.
=
This entire opening sequence is quite different from how it was when Nolan first covered it. I remember it starting out with the village immediately getting attacked, not with Sarah having a girl chat in the cave with Llewl. So that’s interesting.
=
I think it would benefit you if you removed the strange “click to proceed” function that happens on the equipment menu. Have the cursor appear directly on the equip slots.
=
The gameplay change with throwing the snowballs at the bird is… interesting. Not good or bad. Just kinda weird. I don’t get the point of having it. Maybe put in a mechanical reason for hitting the bird before a timer runs out so it’s weaker in the boss fight, or if you mess it up and let it go for too long, Hans gets hurt going into the boss fight.
Spoiler:
Cons
-
For as much as I appreciate that (most of) the SFX is custom, the actual SFX used is a bit weak. Like when Sarah hits enemies with physical attacks, the animation is too slow and the SFX doesn’t feel crunchy or loud enough for it to feel satisfying. It feels like taking a bite from an apple than crushing something. (Which combined with the RTP sound effects other attacks use makes it feel weird. I hope you fix this.)
-
Many of the animations, in fact, feel too slow. Hans uses Chicken Song and his little SFX plays out before the effect is even half over. Sarah uses Light Shot and it has to wait for the entire animation to play with that sparkly effect.
The slowness builds up after a while with all of the enemies you can run into, and it made combat feel unsatisfying.
-
My biggest issue with this combat system, other than the slowness, is that it feels unbalanced. The automatic shield system makes fights with normal enemies very easy, especially with how it regenerates after each fight – which combined with Sarah’s healing skill, makes even bosses easy.
It’s an attempt to make it more interesting + give the player a safety net, but I feel it balances itself way too far into the “cushioned play room” direction.
-
It feels off that Hans starts off with Backstab to move characters forward, yet he needs to level up to get Chicken Song which does the reverse. You want the player to start off with all of the basic tools to understand how your system works.
-
It's strange how you have tooltips yet you don't actually describe what the states do/mean. Like what does Iced mean?
-
Likewise, I don't understand what the Moghunter Combo HUD display is for. Even during the times where attacks did combo into each other, the damage displayed/healed wasn't accurate in the slightest.
-
Stat-wise, all of the enemies take way too long to kill. Generally speaking, you want your starter enemies to die in like, 1-2 hits without any fancy set-up. The boss in particular felt like a grueling damage sponge, since you already figure out how to deal with him: Sacred Fire + Backstab/Chicken Song and the occasional heal and Light Shot.
It felt like his fight went on for like, four turns longer than it should have. Ditto for the normal enemies. (Shoutout to hitting the beginner Snowball enemy four times with the regular attack just to kill it.)
-
Typos:
*
“What are you standing there for silly” is missing a comma after ‘for’.
*
“Don’t worry; Sarah I’ll protect you!” should be “Don’t worry Sarah, I’ll protect you!”
*
“I thought you were the guardian Sarah.” should be “I thought you were the Guardian, Sarah!?” since he’s also… you know, in the talons of a giant ice bird!? I also don’t think he’d be so casual while in this situation. This sequence is also missing a period when he gets to “Just sayin’”.
-
In fact, that entire sequence with the bird boss had the weakest writing. I didn’t find “The Blade” joke to be funny, and it didn’t have the correct emotion for what’s happening? Dude was literally strung up by a giant ice bird a few minutes earlier, and he’s quipping like this is a Marvel movie. Didn’t like that.
- (!!)
The game seems to be a bit resource intensive for my (admittedly bad) laptop.
Spoiler:
Overall Thoughts
Llewl is the game that's gotten the closest to replicating the quintessential "golden era JRPG" out of most of the games I've played - it has the style, the interesting mechanics and it doesn't waste your time too much. (I hope you keep streamlining the rest of the game so it stays character focused instead of throwing loredumps at the player.)
The jumping and swimming and even the snowball throwing makes the game feel alive in a way a lot of RPG Maker games don't even try, which is fascinating. The combat is also pretty cool with its position-based attacks.
But as it is? It doesn't feel like it's there. The shield mechanics complicate the game by making it too easy if you have them but potentially super punishing if you don't, the attack animations are slow enough to make combat feel like a drag, and fighting the actual enemies themselves takes forever because they all have inflated HP values - especially the boss.
It feels like it hasn't hit that perfect middle ground yet. That said, the fact you've gotten this close is exciting. I'd love to see where you go from here.

Thats so much man.  Sorry I'm so late, lifes been crazy last couple of weeks.  This is really brilliant and actionable feedback. Added every single piece to my kanban.
All added to my notes and most of it will be implemented except, the start being ridiculously easy is by design.  The first dungeon is basically a "play about dungeon", then 2nd leans into the armour mechanic more, 3rd positioning mechanic so I felt keeping it facepalm easy was a good idea but I will say feedback on the difficulty has been 50/50.  I might drop enemy HP slightly by maybe 15% and increase damage to compensate, I'll run some tests.
I'll be applying I'd say at least 99% of this, some are in already like backstab is just a backstab now and he uses songs more aptly names to move enemies "Backstep boogie" for backwards and "forward fandango" for forward.
I am working to improve performance a lot, without overstepping tos. Visu plugins hit pretty hard and there's a ton of stuff I'm tempted to drop, like the weather plugin and lighting and just move to regular simple weather system.  So where I can I'm looking for simpler solutions.
Again thanks so much for this dude, I really appreciate it and glad you can see what the exact goal of the game is.  I totally agree we're not quite there yet, closer to what it's supposed to be.
